title: Bleeding and bleeding disorders
subtitle: Approach and lab workup · VWD, hemophilia, rare factor and platelet disorders, acquired inhibitors · products, thresholds, massive hemorrhage, reversal · hemostatic agents and special situations
source: Compiled from the Fellowship Coagulation & Bleeding Disorders, Hemophilia and Transfusion Medicine reviews · ASH/ISTH/NHF/WFH 2021 VWD, WFH 2020, AABB 2023/2025, AABB/ICTMG 2025 guidance · FDA labels · primary trial reports verified against PubMed, October 2026.

blocks.heading: Approach to the bleeding patient
items: History: how did surgery, dental extraction, childbirth, menses and trauma go? Transfusion or iron for bleeding counts. Drugs (antiplatelets, anticoagulants, SSRIs, fish oil), liver/renal disease, family history
ISTH-BAT abnormal at ≥4 in adult men, ≥6 in adult women, ≥3 in children Elbatarny 2014. A low score in a young patient with few challenges does not exclude

Pattern: mucocutaneous (epistaxis, gums, menses, petechiae) → platelets or VWF. Deep tissue (joints, muscle, delayed post-op) → factor deficiency. Delayed bleeding + poor healing → FXIII; fibrinolytic sites (mouth, nose, urinary) → FXI
First-line labs: CBC + smear, PT/INR, aPTT, Clauss fibrinogen, TT; VWF panel even if the aPTT is normal
Pre-analytic traps: heparin from a line, underfilled tube, Hct >55% (excess citrate) falsely prolong clotting times — redraw by clean venipuncture
Stanford: Special Coag lab 650-723-4813 · Transfusion Medicine pager 12027

blocks.heading: PT and aPTT patterns
rows: FVII deficiency; early vitamin K deficiency/warfarin (FVII t½ ~6 h); liver
FVIII, IX, XI deficiency; VWD (low FVIII); acquired hemophilia A; heparin
FXII, prekallikrein, HMWK deficiency; lupus anticoagulant (thrombosis, not bleeding)
FX, V, II or fibrinogen deficiency; DIC; liver disease; severe vitamin K deficiency/warfarin; DOACs; dilution; amyloid (FX)
VWD, platelet function defect or drug, FXIII, α2-antiplasmin/PAI-1, vascular (EDS, HHT, scurvy), mild factor deficiency
blocks.footnote: A normal PT does not exclude apixaban — use a drug-calibrated anti-Xa level.

blocks.heading: Second-line tests
items: Specific factor assays (one-stage, chromogenic for FVIII on emicizumab); Bethesda for inhibitors
VWF panel ± multimers, low-dose RIPA (2B), FVIII-binding (2N)
Platelet function: PFA-100 as a screen, light transmission aggregometry, flow for GPIIb/IIIa and GPIb, electron microscopy for granules
FXIII activity, α2-antiplasmin, PAI-1 when screens are normal
Viscoelastic testing (TEG/ROTEM) for acute bleeding; anti-Xa or drug levels for anticoagulants
Normal full workup + convincing bleeding = bleeding disorder of unknown cause: manage as mild disorder (TXA ± DDAVP trial)

blocks.heading: Mixing study
items: 1:1 with pooled normal plasma. Corrects → deficiency (50% of any factor suffices). Fails to correct → inhibitor
Immediate inhibitor: lupus anticoagulant, heparin (check TT / anti-Xa first)
Time- and temperature-dependent: anti-FVIII autoantibody: corrects at first, prolongs after 1–2 h at 37°C — ask the lab to incubate
Next: factor levels, Bethesda titer, LA testing (dRVVT)

blocks.heading: Rare factor deficiencies
items: FXI: autosomal, common in Ashkenazi Jews; bleeding does not track the level; fibrinolytic sites (mouth, nose, urinary). TXA ± plasma
FXIII: PT and aPTT normal. Umbilical stump, delayed bleeding, poor healing, ICH. Quantitative FXIII activity (clot solubility is insensitive); monthly FXIII concentrate
FVII: isolated ↑PT; bleeding correlates poorly with level; rFVIIa 15–30 µg/kg
Fibrinogen: dysfibrinogenemia can bleed or clot (low Clauss, ↑TT); fibrinogen concentrate
α2-antiplasmin / PAI-1: normal screens, delayed bleeding → TXA

blocks.heading: Von Willebrand disease — ASH/ISTH/NHF/WFH 2021
items: Most common inherited bleeding disorder; mucocutaneous bleeding, heavy menses, postpartum hemorrhage
Panel: VWF:Ag, platelet-binding activity (VWF:GPIbM or GPIbR preferred over VWF:RCo), FVIII; multimers if activity:Ag <0.7
Diagnose type 1 at VWF <0.30 IU/mL regardless of bleeding, or <0.50 with abnormal bleeding. Activity:Ag <0.7 → type 2
Levels move: stress, inflammation, pregnancy, estrogen raise VWF; group O runs ~25% lower. Repeat before excluding; levels that normalize with age → reconsider, don't remove, the diagnosis

Rx: DDAVP trial (VWF + FVIII at baseline, 1 h, 4 h) → responders use it for minor procedures · TXA for mucosal bleeding · VWF concentrate (plasma-derived or recombinant vonicog alfa) for type 3, 2B, non-responders, major surgery · hormonal therapy or TXA for heavy menses

blocks.heading: VWD types
rows: Gain-of-function GPIb binding → HMW loss + low platelets; ↑ low-dose RIPA; exclude platelet-type (GP1BA)
Low FVIII, near-normal VWF — mimics mild hemophilia A but autosomal

blocks.heading: VWD — procedures and pregnancy
items: Major surgery: VWF activity and FVIII both ≥0.50 IU/mL for ≥3 days
Minor procedures: raise VWF to ≥0.50 (DDAVP or concentrate) + TXA; type 1 with VWF >0.30 and mild phenotype → TXA alone
Neuraxial anesthesia: target VWF activity 0.50–1.50; keep >0.50 while the catheter is in and ≥6 h after removal. Check levels in the third trimester
Postpartum: TXA for type 1 or low VWF (reasonable in types 2 and 3)
Give antiplatelets or anticoagulants when truly indicated; VWD is not a contraindication

blocks.heading: Acquired von Willebrand syndrome
items: Shear destroys HMW multimers: aortic stenosis (Heyde: angiodysplasia bleeding, resolves after valve replacement), LVAD (near-universal), ECMO
Adsorption onto platelets: MPN with very high counts (ET >1,000k) → hold aspirin, cytoreduce
Antibody / clearance: MGUS and lymphoproliferative disease (IgG MGUS responds to IVIG), SLE, hypothyroidism
Clue: low activity:Ag ratio, lost HMW multimers, short DDAVP response

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — hemophilia, acquired hemophilia, platelet disorders, products, thresholds, massive hemorrhage, reversal

blocks.heading: Hemophilia A and B
items: X-linked; A (FVIII) ~1 in 5,000 males, B (FIX) ~1 in 25,000–30,000. Joints, muscle, ICH; ↑aPTT that corrects
Severity by factor level: severe <1% (spontaneous bleeds) · moderate 1–5% · mild >5–<40% (bleeds with trauma, surgery). Carriers can bleed — check a level before surgery or delivery
Acute bleed: replace first, image second. CNS/life-threatening FVIII 80–100%, FIX 60–80%, joint 40–60% WFH 2020. FVIII 1 U/kg → ↑~2%, FIX → ↑~1%
Inhibitors (~25–30% of severe A, rare in B): ≥5 BU = high titer → bypassing agents (rFVIIa, aPCC); immune tolerance to eradicate
Emicizumab (IXa–X bispecific): SC prophylaxis for A ± inhibitors (HAVEN 1, 3), not for acute bleeds. Normalizes the aPTT and corrupts one-stage FVIII/Bethesda assays → use bovine chromogenic assays
Also: extended-half-life factor, anti-TFPI (marstacimab, concizumab), fitusiran (antithrombin siRNA), gene therapy. DDAVP for mild A only

blocks.heading: Acquired hemophilia A
items: Autoantibody to FVIII. Elderly, postpartum, autoimmune, cancer; ~half idiopathic
New extensive soft-tissue bleeding (ecchymoses, muscle, retroperitoneum); joints rare. ↑aPTT not correcting after incubation, low FVIII, Bethesda titer (does not predict bleeding)

Stop the bleed: recombinant porcine FVIII (Obizur; 200 U/kg, then by FVIII level) or bypassing agents — rFVIIa 90 µg/kg q2–3 h or aPCC 50–100 U/kg (max 200 U/kg/day). Emicizumab prophylaxis is off-label in the US (approved in Japan 2022)
Eradicate at diagnosis: prednisone 1 mg/kg ± cyclophosphamide or rituximab; seek the cause

blocks.heading: Platelet function disorders
rows: GPIIb/IIIa (ITGA2B/ITGB3), recessive; normal count. LTA: no aggregation to any agonist except ristocetin. Platelets (HLA-matched if alloimmunized); rFVIIa if refractory
GPIb-IX-V; giant platelets + low count (often mislabeled ITP). Absent ristocetin response, not corrected by normal plasma
δ-granule: absent secondary wave (Hermansky-Pudlak with albinism; Chediak-Higashi). α-granule: gray platelet syndrome (NBEAL2). DDAVP often helps
Antiplatelets, uremia, MPN, bypass, SSRIs, paraprotein
blocks.footnote: PFA-100 catches VWD and severe defects, misses storage pool and mild defects; invalid if plt <100k or Hct <30%. Light transmission aggregometry is the reference test; bleeding time is obsolete.

blocks.heading: Blood products
rows: ~300 mL, Hct ~55–65%. 1 unit → Hb ↑ ~1 g/dL in a non-bleeding adult. Single units, then reassess
1 apheresis unit ≈ pool of 4–6 whole-blood units. 1 unit → ↑ ~30k (less with fever, sepsis, splenomegaly, refractoriness). Dose doesn't change bleeding (PLADO)
All coagulation factors. 10–15 mL/kg (~4 units in 70 kg) for a real coagulopathy; TACO risk
Fibrinogen, FVIII, VWF, FXIII. 10 units (2 pools of 5) → fibrinogen ↑ ~70–100 mg/dL

blocks.heading: RBC thresholds — AABB 2023
rows: Liberal <10 g/dL AABB 2025 conditional; ACC/AHA 2025 2b. MINT: MI/death 16.9% restrictive vs 14.5% liberal, RR 1.15, P=0.07 — favored, not proven

blocks.heading: Platelet thresholds — AABB/ICTMG 2025
blocks.footnote: Avoid platelets in TTP/HIT unless life-threatening bleeding; ITP only for serious bleeding, with IVIG + steroids; useless in PTP; harmful in antiplatelet ICH (PATCH).

blocks.heading: Massive hemorrhage
items: Activate the MTP; T&S, CBC, PT/aPTT, fibrinogen, iCa, ABG, lactate every 30–60 min
1:1:1 plasma : platelets : RBC — PROPPR vs 1:1:2: 30-d mortality not different (22.4% vs 26.1%), but hemostasis 86% vs 78% and exsanguination death at 24 h 9.2% vs 14.6%
TXA 1 g over 10 min + 1 g over 8 h, within 3 h (CRASH-2). After 3 h bleeding deaths rose (RR 1.44) — don't start late
Fibrinogen >150–200 mg/dL (cryo or concentrate); replace ionized calcium early (citrate); prevent hypothermia and correct acidosis
Viscoelastic testing (TEG/ROTEM): long R/CT → plasma; low MA/MCF → platelets or fibrinogen (FIBTEM); high LY30 → TXA
Reverse anticoagulants; prehospital plasma in long air transport (PAMPer)

blocks.heading: Anticoagulant and antiplatelet reversal
rows: 4F-PCC 25 / 35 / 50 U/kg for INR 2–<4 / 4–6 / >6 (max 2500 / 3500 / 5000 U) or fixed 1000–1500 U, + vitamin K 10 mg IV. PCC beats plasma: rapid INR correction 62% vs 10% (Sarode 2013); in ICH, INR ≤1.2 by 3 h 67% vs 9% (INCH). No bleeding, INR >10 → oral vitamin K
Idarucizumab 5 g IV (REVERSE-AD: median reversal 100%); dialyzable. Normal TT excludes a relevant level

4F-PCC 25–50 U/kg or fixed 2000 U (off-label). Andexanet left the US market 22 Dec 2025 — FDA judged thrombotic risk to outweigh benefit (ANNEXA-I: thrombosis 10.3% vs 5.6%, ischemic stroke 6.5% vs 1.5%). Charcoal if ingested <2–4 h
Protamine 1 mg per 100 U given in the last 2–3 h (max 50 mg); check aPTT
Enoxaparin ≤8 h: protamine 1 mg/mg; 8–12 h: 0.5 mg/mg (max 50 mg). Partial (~60% of anti-Xa)
No platelet transfusion in ICH (PATCH: death or dependence OR 2.05) unless neurosurgery; DDAVP 0.4 µg/kg ×1 an option (NCS/SCCM 2016)
Stop; cryo 10 units (fibrinogen ≥150); TXA 1 g or aminocaproic acid 4–5 g

blocks.heading: Plasma and cryo — when
items: Plasma for: bleeding + coagulopathy (liver, DIC, dilution), massive transfusion, TTP plasma exchange, a factor deficiency without a concentrate (FV)
Don't correct an INR <1.7 with plasma before a procedure: little effect, added TACO and TRALI risk. Not a volume expander; not for warfarin reversal when PCC is available
Cryo or fibrinogen concentrate: fibrinogen <150 mg/dL with bleeding (DIC, MTP, APL; <200 in obstetric hemorrhage)

pages.subtitle: Page 3 — hemostatic agents, special situations, key trials

blocks.heading: Hemostatic agents — dosing
rows: 1 g IV over 10 min (trauma + 1 g over 8 h; PPH repeat at 30 min if bleeding). PO 1300 mg TID × 5 d (menses); 5% mouthwash. Renal dosing. Aminocaproic acid 4–5 g then 1 g/h is the alternative
Mucosal, dental, menses, trauma, PPH, surgery. Avoid in upper urinary tract bleeding (ureteral clots). No benefit in GI bleeding, more VTE (HALT-IT)
Type 1 VWD, mild hemophilia A, carriers, uremia, platelet dysfunction. Tachyphylaxis after 2–3 doses; restrict fluids 24 h, check Na; caution CAD, age <2. Avoid in 2B
Cryo 10 units → ↑70–100 mg/dL. Concentrate (RiaSTAP, Fibryga): mg/kg = (target − measured mg/dL) ÷ 1.7 (RiaSTAP); ÷ 1.8 Fibryga (÷ 1.4 if <12 y)
II, VII, IX, X + C/S + heparin — avoid in HIT
Inhibitors (congenital or acquired). On emicizumab: >100 U/kg/24 h for ≥24 h → TMA, thrombosis
Inhibitors / AHA: 90 µg/kg q2–3 h. FVII deficiency: 15–30 µg/kg q4–6 h
Licensed: hemophilia with inhibitors, FVII deficiency, Glanzmann refractory to platelets, acquired hemophilia. Off-label rescue: no mortality benefit, ↑ arterial thrombosis
10 mg IV slowly for bleeding; 1–5 mg PO non-urgent
IV acts in hours (full 12–24 h); avoid SC. Rare anaphylactoid reaction
FVIII U = kg × desired % rise ÷ 2. FIX U = kg × desired % rise (÷ ~0.8 for some recombinant FIX)
Recheck trough; extended-half-life products dosed less often
3 mg/kg SC weekly ×4, then 1.5 mg/kg weekly, 3 mg/kg q2wk or 6 mg/kg q4wk
Uremic bleeding; onset ~1 d, effect lasts ~2 wk

blocks.heading: Heavy menstrual bleeding
items: Screen for a bleeding disorder when heavy menses date from menarche, or with iron deficiency or postpartum hemorrhage
VWD: hormonal therapy (combined contraception or levonorgestrel IUS) or TXA, preferred over DDAVP ASH/ISTH 2021
Treat iron deficiency in parallel (IV iron if oral fails)

blocks.heading: Patients who decline blood
items: Ask product by product — many Jehovah's Witnesses accept albumin, factor concentrates, PCC, fibrinogen concentrate or cell salvage; document it
Build reserve, cut losses: IV iron ± ESA, TXA, pediatric tubes and fewer draws, early reversal of anticoagulants

blocks.heading: Special situations
rows: Rebalanced hemostasis; INR does not predict procedural bleeding — don't give plasma to fix it. Fibrinogen and platelets matter more when bleeding; TEG/ROTEM. TPO-RA (avatrombopag, lusutrombopag) before procedures if plt <50k. Variceal bleeding is portal pressure — avoid volume
Dialysis; raise Hb toward ~10 (improves platelet margination); DDAVP 0.3 µg/kg for acute bleeds or procedures; conjugated estrogens for longer effect; cryo if refractory
Treat the cause. Products only for bleeding or procedures: plt >50k, fibrinogen >150 mg/dL, plasma 15–30 mL/kg for prolonged PT/aPTT. ISTH score ≥5 = overt. Heparin only when thrombosis dominates
TXA routinely; protamine for heparin rebound; viscoelastic-guided algorithms reduce transfusion; bypass causes platelet dysfunction; acquired VWS on ECMO/LVAD

TXA 1 g IV within 3 h (WOMAN: bleeding death 1.5% vs 1.9%, RR 0.81; ≤3 h RR 0.69). Fibrinogen ≤2 g/L predicts severe PPH (PPV 100%, Charbit 2007) → keep >2 g/L. Abruption and amniotic fluid embolism → DIC
Coagulopathy is the early killer: start ATRA on suspicion; keep fibrinogen >100–150 mg/dL and plt >30–50k with cryo and platelets; avoid invasive procedures

Reverse now: 4F-PCC + vitamin K for warfarin; idarucizumab or PCC for DOACs. SBP target ~140, avoid <130 AHA/ASA 2022. No platelets for antiplatelet ICH (PATCH). rFVIIa not recommended (FAST, FASTEST)
TXA ≤3 h (CRASH-2); TBI: head-injury death ↓ in mild–moderate injury (CRASH-3, RR 0.78); 1:1:1 (PROPPR); prehospital plasma (PAMPer)
Major surgery: FVIII 80–100% / FIX 60–80% pre-op, then taper over 1–2 wk (WFH 2020); dental: TXA mouthwash + factor. Plan with the hemophilia treatment center

blocks.heading: ISTH overt DIC score
blocks.footnote: Score ≥5 = overt DIC; repeat daily. Only in a patient with a condition known to cause DIC Taylor 2001.

blocks.heading: Key trials
rows: Trauma TXA (n=20,211): death 14.5% vs 16.0%, RR 0.91; harm if started >3 h
TBI TXA ≤3 h: head-injury death 18.5% vs 19.8% (NS); mild–moderate RR 0.78
1:1:1 vs 1:1:2: mortality NS; hemostasis 86% vs 78%, exsanguination 9.2% vs 14.6%
Prehospital plasma, air transport: 30-d mortality 23.2% vs 33.0%
PPH TXA (n=20,060): bleeding death 1.5% vs 1.9% (RR 0.81); no ↑ thrombosis
GI bleeding TXA: bleeding death 4% vs 4% (RR 0.99); VTE 0.8% vs 0.4% → don't use
Platelets for antiplatelet ICH: death/dependence OR 2.05 → don't transfuse
rFVIIa in ICH: less hematoma growth, no functional benefit; arterial events 9% vs 4%; FASTEST stopped for futility, thromboembolism RR 3.41
4F-PCC vs plasma for warfarin bleeding: hemostasis 72% vs 65% (non-inferior), rapid INR correction 62% vs 10%; ICH: INR ≤1.2 in 3 h 67% vs 9%
ICU Hb 7 vs 10: 30-d mortality 18.7% vs 23.3% (P=0.11) → restrictive is safe
Hip fracture + CV risk, Hb 10 vs <8/symptoms: death or inability to walk 35.2% vs 34.7%
Septic shock, Hb 7 vs 9: 90-d mortality 43.0% vs 45.0%
Acute MI, restrictive vs liberal <10: MI/death 16.9% vs 14.5%, RR 1.15, P=0.07
AML induction, plt 10k vs 20k: major bleeding 21.5% vs 20%; 21.5% fewer transfusions
No prophylactic platelets: WHO ≥2 bleeding 50% vs 43% → keep 10k prophylaxis
Andexanet vs usual care, Xa-inhibitor ICH: hemostasis 67% vs 53%; thrombosis 10.3% vs 5.6% → withdrawn in US
Emicizumab: annualized bleeds 2.9 vs 23.3 with inhibitors (−87%); 1.5 vs 38.2 without (−96%)
